stem: During routine tracheostomy care, which action is appropriate for the nurse?

options.A: Inspect the stoma for redness or drainage, clean the site, and maintain the inner cannula according to the device and agency procedure
options.B: Allow secretions to accumulate around the stoma to avoid disturbing the site
options.C: Cover the tracheostomy opening with an occlusive dressing during routine care
options.D: Ignore a wet or soiled tracheostomy dressing until the next scheduled day

rationale: Open RN Nursing Skills, 2nd edition, describes routine tracheostomy care as keeping the flange, dressing, ties, inner cannula, and surrounding area clean. It directs inspection of the stoma for redness, drainage, and infection and maintenance of the inner cannula to prevent obstruction.
educational_objective: Perform routine tracheostomy care with stoma assessment, cleanliness, and airway-patency maintenance.
source_document_title: Nursing Skills, 2nd edition — Chapter 22 Tracheostomy Care & Suctioning
source_locator: 22.6 Checklist for Tracheostomy Care; inspect drainage/stoma and clean/replace inner cannula as indicated
source_claim_supported: Supports routine cleaning, inspection for redness/drainage/infection, dressing care, and inner-cannula maintenance.
correction_summary: Removed an overly generic 'leave it alone' contrast and tied the correct answer to explicit stoma and inner-cannula care actions.
audit_findings: A is directly source-supported. B and D permit contamination/skin problems; C would obstruct the artificial airway.
blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Basic Care and Comfort, printed p.11 / PDF p.15
